title: How a Microsoft Azure tenant, management group or subscription is onboarded to DSPM, and the Azure roles and API permissions it needs

checks.do: Which prerequisite roles the tenant or management group page lists, and which roles the subscription page lists for deploying the templates.
Which Microsoft Graph permissions the subscription page marks Mandatory or Optional, and the permissions the IAM roles page lists as required for the DSPM service principal.
Whether the orchestrator network configuration is Zscaler or Custom: only Zscaler-mode tenants can change the orchestrator subscription, and Unmanaged Database is disabled for Zscaler.

tenant-scope.statement: You can onboard a Microsoft Entra tenant or management group and their associated subscriptions; DSPM monitors and scans the data stores (for example databases, virtual machines, storage accounts) in the onboarded subscriptions for sensitive data, misconfigurations and vulnerabilities.

quotes: You can onboard a Microsoft Entra tenant or management group and their associated subscriptions.
DSPM monitors and scans the data stores (e.g., databases, virtual machines, storage accounts) in the onboarded subscriptions to identify sensitive data, misconfigurations, and vulnerabilities.

tenant-azure-roles.statement: The tenant onboarding prerequisites table lists Global Administrator at Root for tenant or management group onboarding, User Access Administrator at Root for tenant onboarding, and for management group onboarding Contributor on the orchestrator subscription and User Access Administrator on the management group; Key Vault Administrator is also required.

quotes: | Tenant or Management group | Global Administrator | Root |
| Tenant | User Access Administrator | Root |
| Management group | Contributor | Orchestrator subscription |
| User Access Administrator | Management group |  |
The Key Vault Administrator role is required to perform operations on a key vault that stores secrets such as passwords, certificates, etc. and all objects in it.

tenant-vm-size.statement: The orchestrator region must offer the Standard_D2s_v3 virtual machine instance type, which is required to run the orchestrator instance.

quotes: Virtual machine instance type: Ensure that you have the Standard_D2s_v3 virtual machine instance type in the region where the orchestrator template must be deployed. This is required to run the orchestrator instance.

tenant-access-mgmt-and-provider.statement: Tenant onboarding requires Access management for Azure resources to be enabled (to manage access to all subscriptions and management groups in the tenant) and the Microsoft.Storage resource provider registered in the orchestrator template subscription (so DSPM can validate the storage account created while onboarding).

quotes: Access management: Enable Access management for Azure resources. This is required to manage access to all subscriptions and management groups in the tenant.

Microsoft Storage Resource Provider: Register the Microsoft Azure Storage Resource Provider (Microsoft.Storage) in the subscription within which the orchestrator template is deployed. This is required for DSPM to validate the storage account created while onboarding.

tenant-state-files.statement: Terraform state files must be stored in an identified storage container; they are required to manage resources created by the DSPM Terraform templates and to upgrade to new templates, and if they are lost or deleted the resources must be purged and the onboarding templates downloaded and rerun.

quotes: Storage containers: Identify the storage containers where Terraform state files must be stored. The state files are required to manage resources created by the DSPM Terraform templates and to upgrade to new templates.
Ensure to store the state files safely to upgrade to new templates. If the state files are lost or accidentally deleted, purge the resources, download and rerun the onboarding templates.

tenant-tool-versions.statement: The page says to install the latest versions and tabulates the versions it was captured with: Mac Terraform v1.10.3 and Azure CLI 2.65.0; Cloud Shell (Bash and PowerShell) Terraform v1.9.5 and Azure CLI 2.65.0; Windows command line Terraform v1.7.5 and Azure CLI 2.67.0; Windows PowerShell Terraform v1.9.8 and Azure CLI 2.67.0.

quotes: Install the latest versions
| Mac | v1.10.3 | 2.65.0 | version 3.2.57(1)-release (arm64-apple-darwin23) |
| Cloud Shell - Bash | v1.9.5 | 2.65.0 | version 5.1.8(1)-release (x86_64-pc-linux-gnu) |
| Cloud Shell - PowerShell | v1.9.5 | 2.65.0 | 7.4.5 |
| Windows - Command line | v1.7.5 | 2.67.0 | NA |
| Windows - PowerShell | v1.9.8 | 2.67.0 | 7.4.6 |

tenant-debug-logs.statement: Zscaler recommends enabling Terraform debug logs while onboarding, by setting TF_LOG to TRACE and TF_LOG_PATH to a log file path.

quotes: Zscaler recommends you to enable the debug logs feature to identify issues encountered while onboarding.
$env:TF_LOG="TRACE" $env:TF_LOG_PATH="<filepath>filename.log"
export TF_LOG="TRACE" $ export TF_LOG_PATH="<filepath>filename.log"

tenant-admin-console-role.statement: Onboarding requires an Administrator role or any role with Add Accounts permissions in the Zscaler Admin Console.

quotes: You must be assigned either an Administrator role or any role with Add Accounts permissions in the Zscaler Admin Console.

tenant-cleanup-resources.statement: A cleanup procedure in the tenant prerequisites lists resources to delete or purge in Azure: resource groups z-dspm-{integration-id}-auth-plane-rg, -worker-plane-rg and -control-plane-rg, key vaults named z-dspm-{integration-id}-secrets to purge, and the roles <role_name>-access-role, -analyzer-role, -orchestrator-role and <role_name>-target-role.

quotes: - z-dspm-{integration-id}-auth-plane-rg
- z-dspm-{integration-id}-worker-plane-rg
- z-dspm-{integration-id}-control-plane-rg
- z-dspm-{integration-id}-secrets
- <role_name>-access-role
- <role_name>-analyzer-role
- <role_name>-orchestrator-role
Delete <role_name>-target-role from all the target subscriptions.

tenant-details-fields.statement: In the Tenant Details step the role name and service principal name may contain only letters, numbers, hyphens and underscores; the role name is a prefix for all custom roles created during onboarding; the Management Group ID field is shown only for management group onboarding and accepts several IDs; Notification Emails is optional and takes up to 30 addresses.

quotes: The role name and service principal name must contain only alphabetic characters, numbers, hyphens ("-"), and underscores ("_").
This role name is added as a prefix to all the custom roles that are created during the onboarding process.
You can include multiple management group IDs to onboard the management groups.
This field is visible only if you select the Management Group for onboarding.
Notification Emails (Optional): Enter the email addresses of the recipients who must be notified of any configuration or permissions issues encountered with the onboarded tenant.
You can add up to 30 email addresses to receive notifications about the issues.

tree-discovery-template.statement: The tree discovery template includes policies and permissions to create the service principal, a resource discovery role and managed identities, and generates the application ID and client secret; its ZIP holds two Terraform files (backend.tf and azure_tf_basic.tf).

quotes: Includes policies and permissions to create the service principal, resource discovery role with required permissions, and managed identities.
Generates the application ID and client secret that are required for the service principal to connect to the Microsoft Entra tenant.
The ZIP file contains two Terraform files (backend.tf and azure_tf_basic.tf).

tree-discovery-consent-validate.statement: After deploying the tree discovery template, API permissions must be granted to the service principal through admin consent in Microsoft Entra ID; validation in the Admin Console verifies the application ID, client secret and the custom roles created, and on an error the template is rerun.

quotes: You need to grant API permissions to the service principal to access resources within the tenant.
Click Grant admin consent for <tenant name>.
DSPM validates the template deployment by verifying the application ID, client secret, and the custom roles created.
If there is any issue while deploying the template, an error is displayed. Rerun the template.

tree-discovery-ai-role.statement: If AI service data collection is enabled, the Custom Role (AI Agent) is assigned to the Tree Discovery service principal at the subscription level.

quotes: If AI service data collection is enabled, assign the Custom Role (AI Agent) to this Tree Discovery service principal at the subscription level.

network-config.statement: On the tenant or management group orchestrator and monitoring scope page, network configuration is Zscaler (Zscaler resources) or Custom (the organization's resources); Custom is selected by default and the Zscaler configuration requires contacting Zscaler Support.

quotes: Zscaler: Use Zscaler resources to deploy the orchestrator and monitoring scope.
Custom: Use your organization's resources to deploy the orchestrator and monitoring scope.
By default, the custom configuration is selected. If you want to use the Zscaler configuration, contact Zscaler Support.

orch-storage-account-name.statement: In the Zscaler network configuration text, the orchestrator storage account name must not exceed 16 characters; DSPM shows an error if the name is already registered with Microsoft.Storage.

quotes: DSPM validates the uniqueness of the storage account name. If the name is already registered with Microsoft.Storage, DSPM displays an error message.
The storage account name must not exceed 16 characters.

orch-private-endpoint.statement: The Deploy private endpoint for secure communication checkbox establishes a private connection between DSPM and Azure resources and restricts communication over public IP addresses; it can be set or removed after onboarding.

quotes: Select the Deploy private endpoint for secure communication checkbox to establish a private connection between DSPM and Azure resources. This restricts communication over public IP addresses.
You can also establish or remove the private connection after onboarding the tenant.

services-to-monitor.statement: On the tenant or management group services page all services are selected by default and DSPM permissions are restricted to monitoring and scanning only the selected services; Azure Storage accounts used for storing logs are excluded automatically, and the Leverage MIP Label checkbox allows applying MIP sensitivity labels to Azure File Share.

quotes: By default, all the services are selected. DSPM permissions are restricted to monitor and scan the data only in the selected services.
DSPM automatically excludes Azure Storage accounts used for storing logs.
Select the Leverage MIP Label checkbox to allow DSPM to apply Microsoft Information Protection (MIP) sensitivity labels to Azure File Share.

unmanaged-db-zscaler-network.statement: In tenant or management group onboarding, the Unmanaged Database service is disabled for Zscaler network configuration.

quotes: The Unmanaged Database service is disabled for Zscaler network configuration.

regions-and-custom-network-fields.statement: DSPM creates and deploys scanning resources only in the selected regions, which must be specified again when deploying the orchestrator template; with Custom network configuration each region takes a Subnet ID and Network Security Group ID, and the optional Postgres Delegated Subnet ID is available only if Database was selected.

quotes: DSPM creates and deploys resources required for scanning only in the selected regions.
Remember the regions that you selected as you need to specify them while deploying the orchestrator template.
Subnet ID: Enter the subnet where the scanner instances must be launched.
Network Security Group ID: Enter the network security group for the scanner instance.
Postgres Delegated Subnet ID: (Optional) Enter the Postgres subnet ID for the scanner instance. This option is available only if Database was selected on the Select which services to monitor page.

custom-scan-log-storage.statement: With Custom network configuration, the per-region storage account creation option can be disabled to supply existing storage account details for scan logs, and it is available only if Storage was selected on the services page.

quotes: If you want to use your own existing storage account for scanning logs, disable this option and provide storage account details for each region.
This option is available only if Storage was selected on the Select which services to monitor page.

monitoring-scope-autodetect.statement: Selecting Autodetection at the management group level makes DSPM automatically include and scan new subscriptions added to the management group; all subscriptions in the group are mapped to the business unit assigned to it, the default business unit is assigned initially, and it can be changed after onboarding.

quotes: Select Autodetection at the management group level if you want DSPM to automatically include and scan new subscriptions that are added to the management group in the future.
All the subscriptions within the management group are mapped to the selected business unit.
The default business unit is assigned to the management group. You can change the business unit for the management group if required, after completing the onboarding process.

custom-tags.statement: Custom tags are attached to resources created by DSPM; up to 15 tags can be added to Private DNS zone resources, numeric-only values do not count toward that limit, and Managed Identity resources get only predefined tags.

quotes: Custom tags are attached to resources created by DSPM for easy identification.
You can add up to 15 tags to Private DNS zone resources.
If only numerical values are included in the tag, they do not count towards the 15-tag limit, allowing for additional tags to be added.
For Managed Identity, only predefined tags are added.

evidence-storage.statement: Evidence storage holds snippets of evidence data for files and tables containing sensitive data; the container cannot be changed after it is added, a Custom Managed Container takes a key vault resource ID used to encrypt the evidence data, and a Zscaler Managed Container is created in the orchestrator account.

quotes: DSPM discovers files and tables containing sensitive data and generates snippets of evidence data to investigate and validate the findings.
The storage account container cannot be changed after it is added.
Key Vault Resource ID: The resource ID of the key vault. This key vault is used to encrypt the evidence data in the container.
DSPM creates a storage container in the orchestrator account to upload the snippet of evidence data.
Custom Managed Container
Zscaler Managed Container

onboarding-template-resources.statement: Deploying the Azure onboarding template creates custom roles for orchestrator, target and scanner, virtual machine scale sets for the orchestrator, blob containers for diagnostic logs, a queue receiving scan requests from DSPM, VNET peering and a NAT gateway.

quotes: Custom role for orchestrator: Custom role for orchestrator instance.
Custom role for target: Custom role for target accounts.
Custom role for scanner: Custom role for scanner instance.
Virtual machine scale sets: Scale sets for orchestrator instance.
Blob containers for storing diagnostic logs
Queue to receive scan requests from DSPM. The storage account is created to receive communication from DSPM IPs.
VNET peering: Virtual network peering used to ensure that the communication between orchestrator and scanners are private.
NAT gateway: Network address translation gateway used to provide outbound internet connectivity to orchestrator or scanner instances.

onboarding-template-prompts-validate.statement: Running the Azure onboarding template prompts for the IPv4 address of the system running Terraform; DSPM validates the deployment every hour by checking the roles created and permissions granted, and Validate takes a couple of minutes.

quotes: Enter the IPv4 address from which terraform is being run from: Enter the public IP address of the system on which you are running the template, and press Enter.
DSPM validates the template deployment every hour by checking the roles created and permissions granted.
Click Validate to verify if the template is deployed. This process takes a couple of minutes to complete.

change-orchestrator-scope.statement: Changing the orchestrator subscription applies when the existing subscription is being decommissioned or deleted or was selected incorrectly, and is available only for tenants onboarded through Zscaler network configuration mode.

quotes: You can change the orchestrator subscription if the existing orchestrator subscription is being decommissioned, deleted, or if an incorrect subscription was selected while onboarding.
This option is available only for tenants onboarded through Zscaler network configuration mode.

change-orchestrator-effects.statement: Until the new orchestrator subscription is validated, the existing orchestrator is disabled, the connection status is Waiting for Connection, the configuration status is Pending, data scans stop and the target subscriptions are Needs Attention; after successful deployment the subscriptions return to Successfully Configured and scanning begins.

quotes: The existing orchestrator is disabled.
The DSPM connection status moves to the Waiting for Connection state and Configuration status moves to the Pending state.
The data scans are stopped.
The target subscriptions move to the Needs Attention state.
After the template is successfully deployed, the onboarded subscriptions move to the Successfully Configured state and DSPM begins the data scan.

change-orchestrator-prereqs.statement: Changing the orchestrator subscription requires an administrator role or a role with the Configure New Orchestrator permission, and the system IP address added to the Azure storage account and Key Vault IP networks before redeploying (needed when multiple users apply Terraform from different IP addresses); the previous template is purged with terraform destroy and the random_seed in terraform.tfvars is changed.

quotes: Be assigned either an administrator role or any role with the Configure New Orchestrator permission in the Zscaler Admin Console.
Before redeploying the orchestrator template, you must add your system's IP address to the Azure storage account and Azure Key Vault's IP networks.
This is required when multiple users need to apply Terraform from different IP addresses.
Before running the template on the new orchestrator subscription, purge the previously deployed template by running the terraform destroy command.
terraform.tfvars: Change the random_seed value.

monitoring-scope-no-remove.statement: Once a subscription is added to the monitoring scope it cannot be removed from it; to stop monitoring, the subscription must be deleted from the DSPM tenant. Managing the scope requires an Administrator role or a custom role with the Configure Monitoring Scope permission.

quotes: After a subscription has been added to the monitoring scope, you cannot remove it from the monitoring scope.
If you want to stop monitoring a subscription, you need to delete the subscription from the DSPM tenant.
You must be assigned either an Administrator role or a custom role with the Configure Monitoring Scope permission in the Zscaler Admin Console.

monitoring-scope-autodetection-enable.statement: The monitoring scope can be extended with Autodetection, which lets DSPM automatically detect and onboard new subscriptions added in the future.

quotes: You can also enable autodetection, which allows DSPM to automatically detect and onboard any new subscriptions that are added in the future.

service-principal-deleted.statement: If the service principal is accidentally deleted, DSPM access to the tenant is impacted and all onboarded subscriptions move to Needs Attention; updating the application details restores access and the subscriptions move to Successfully Configured.

quotes: If the service principal is accidentally deleted, DSPM's access to the onboarded tenant is impacted, and all the onboarded subscriptions within the tenant move to the Needs Attention state. To restore access, you must update the application details.
You must be assigned either an Administrator role or any role with Change Application Details permissions.
After the template is successfully deployed, DSPM's access to the Microsoft Entra tenant is restored, and the onboarded subscriptions move to the Successfully Configured state.

client-secret-update-tenant.statement: A service principal client secret has an expiration date and must be renewed for the service principal to remain functional, and the secret provided while onboarding a tenant can be updated; validation of an updated secret shows an error if it is invalid or does not match the service principal.

quotes: You can update the client secret ID that you provided while onboarding a tenant.
It comes with an expiration date and must be renewed for the service principal to remain functional.
If the client secret is invalid, or it does not match the service principal, an error is displayed.
You must be assigned either an Administrator role or any role with Change Application Details permissions in the Zscaler Admin Console.

client-secret-update-subscription.statement: The client secret of the application created while onboarding an Azure subscription has an expiration date and must be renewed for the application to retain DSPM access; validation checks it against the application ID and shows an error if it is invalid or does not match the application.

quotes: You can update the client secret for the application you created while onboarding an Azure subscription.
It comes with an expiration date and must be renewed for the application to retain DSPM's access.
DSPM validates the updated client secret by verifying it against the application ID.
If the client secret is invalid, or it does not match the application, an error is displayed.

subscription-onboarding-scope.statement: A single Azure subscription can be onboarded for DSPM to monitor and scan its data stores for sensitive data, misconfigurations and vulnerabilities; the application (client) ID is saved from the Entra ID app registration because onboarding requires it.

quotes: You can onboard a single Azure subscription for DSPM to monitor and scan the data stores to identify sensitive data, misconfigurations, and vulnerabilities.
Copy the Application (client) ID and save them on your system as this is required while onboarding.

subscription-graph-permissions.statement: For subscription onboarding the Microsoft Graph permissions Application.Read.All (Application) and User.Read (Delegated) are Mandatory and AuditLog.Read.All, Directory.Read.All, InformationProtectionPolicy.Read.All, Organization.Read.All, Reports.Read.All, RoleManagement.Read.Directory, RoleManagementPolicy.Read.Directory and UserAuthenticationMethod.Read.All (Application) are Optional; entitlements are affected if the optional ones are not configured, and granting admin consent requires the Privileged Role Administrator role.

quotes: | Application.Read.All | Mandatory | Application | Read all applications |
| User.Read | Mandatory | Delegated | Sign in and read user profile |
| AuditLog.Read.All | Optional | Application | Read all audit log data |
| Directory.Read.All | Optional | Application | Read directory data |
| InformationProtectionPolicy.Read.All | Optional | Application | Read all published labels and label policies for an organization |
| Organization.Read.All | Optional | Application | Read organization information |
| Reports.Read.All | Optional | Application | Read all usage reports |
| RoleManagement.Read.Directory | Optional | Application | Read all directory RBAC settings |
| RoleManagementPolicy.Read.Directory | Optional | Application | Read all policies for privileged role assignments of your company's directory |
| UserAuthenticationMethod.Read.All | Optional | Application | Read all users' authentication methods |
Entitlements are affected if the optional API permissions are not configured.
You must have the Privileged Role Administrator role in the Microsoft Entra ID to grant API permissions.

subscription-role-assignment.statement: For subscription onboarding the User Access Administrator role is assigned to the created application on the orchestrator and target subscriptions with the condition Allow user to assign all roles (highly privileged), repeated for every subscription DSPM monitors.

quotes: Assign the User Access Administrator role to the created application or service principal on the orchestrator and target subscriptions.
for What users can do, select Allow user to assign all roles (highly privileged)
Repeat this for all the subscriptions that you want DSPM to monitor.

subscription-deploy-roles.statement: To deploy the DSPM templates for subscription onboarding: User Access Administrator, Contributor and Key Vault Administrator on the orchestrator subscription; User Access Administrator on target subscriptions; Storage Account Contributor on the backend storage account; Application Administrator in Microsoft Entra ID, required if the MIP service is selected.

quotes: | Orchestrator subscription | User Access Administrator Contributor Key Vault Administrator |
| Target subscriptions | User Access Administrator |
| Backend storage account | Storage Account Contributor |
| Microsoft Entra ID | Application Administrator (Required if MIP service is selected) |

subscription-fields.statement: Subscription onboarding takes a Custom Role Name Prefix added to all custom roles created, optional Notification Emails (up to 30), and a network configuration for the orchestrator: Custom (the organization's resources) or Zscaler (Zscaler resources).

quotes: Custom Role Name Prefix: Enter a unique role name. This role name is added as a prefix to all the custom roles that are created during the onboarding process.
Notification Emails (Optional): Enter the email addresses of the recipients who must be notified of any configuration or permissions issues encountered with the onboarded tenant.
You can add up to 30 email addresses to receive notifications about the issues.
Custom: Select to use your organization's resources to deploy the orchestrator.
Zscaler: Select to use Zscaler resources to deploy the orchestrator.

subscription-diagnostic-logs-evidence.statement: Diagnostic logs identify new, modified or deleted files from monitored storage accounts and are stored with Custom (an existing storage account resource ID per region of the target subscription) or Zscaler (a storage account DSPM creates in the orchestrator subscription after template deployment); evidence is Custom (existing container) or Automated (DSPM creates a container in the orchestrator account), and the Evidence template is available only if evidence is configured.

quotes: Diagnostic logs are used to identify new, modified, or deleted files from monitored storage accounts.
Custom: Enter an existing storage account resource ID in each region of the target subscription to store the scanning logs.
Zscaler: DSPM creates a storage account in the orchestrator subscription after the template is deployed.
Automated: DSPM creates a storage container in the orchestrator account to upload the snippet of evidence data.
This template is available only if you have configured evidence.
Custom: Use an existing storage account container to configure evidence data.

add-target-subscriptions.statement: Adding target subscriptions to an onboarded Azure account takes a Subscription ID, an optional Subscription Name and a Business Unit, requires an Administrator role or a custom role with Configure Monitoring Scope, and is followed by deploying the Azure Onboarding template from the Roles and Templates tab.

quotes: Subscription ID: Enter the subscription ID.
Subscription Name (Optional): Enter the subscription name.
Business Unit: Select a business unit for the subscription.
You must be assigned either an Administrator role or a custom role with the Configure Monitoring Scope permission in the Zscaler Admin Console.
On the Roles and Templates tab, click Azure Onboarding template to download and deploy the template.

purpose.statement: The IAM roles and permissions page says the DSPM templates create a service principal (enterprise application), custom roles and managed identities in Microsoft Entra ID (the subscription onboarding page has the user register the application), which DSPM needs to connect to the tenant, discover resources and collect metadata.

quotes: These templates create a service principal (enterprise application), custom roles, and managed identities in Microsoft Entra ID.
DSPM requires these roles to connect to the Microsoft Entra tenant, discover the resources, and collect metadata.
Provide the following details to register an Azure application for DSPM to connect to the Azure subscription and click Apply.

resource-discovery-role.statement: The Resource Discovery Role is assigned at the management group level and identifies resources in the onboarded subscriptions; its permissions are */read, Microsoft.Insights/DiagnosticSettings/read, Microsoft.Insights/eventtypes/values/read, Microsoft.Resources/subscriptions/resourceGroups/read, Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/blobServices/containers/read and Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/listkeys/action.

quotes: DSPM requires the resource discovery role to identify resources within the onboarded subscriptions. This role is assigned at the management group level
| */read | Management group | Actions | To allow read permissions to read the metadata of Azure resources |
| Microsoft.Insights/DiagnosticSettings/read | Management group | Actions | To discover diagnostic settings |
| Microsoft.Insights/eventtypes/values/read | Management group | Actions | To read activity logs |
| Microsoft.Resources/subscriptions/resourceGroups/read | Management group | Actions | To discover Azure resource groups |
| Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/blobServices/containers/read | Management group | Actions | To discover Azure blob containers |
| Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/listkeys/action | Management group | Actions | To discover Azure storage account keys |

access-role.statement: The DSPM Access Role sends data scan requests to the storage account queues used by the orchestrator subscription, is assigned at the DSPM resource group level, and holds Microsoft.Compute permissions virtualMachines/read, virtualMachineScaleSets/deallocate/action, virtualMachineScaleSets/virtualMachines/delete and virtualMachineScaleSets/write.

quotes: DSPM requires the access role to send data scan requests to the storage account queues that are used by the orchestrator subscription. The role is assigned at the DSPM resource group level
| Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/read | DSPM resource group | Actions | To read virtual machines |
| Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachineScaleSets/deallocate/action | DSPM resource group | Actions | To deallocate virtual machine scale set |
| Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachineScaleSets/virtualMachines/delete | DSPM resource group | Actions | To delete virtual machine in a virtual machine scale set |
| Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachineScaleSets/write | DSPM resource group | Actions | To create or update virtual machine scale set |

target-role.statement: The Target Role is required by the orchestrator subscription to scan data stores and is assigned at the monitoring scope or target subscriptions level; its Actions include disks/beginGetAccess/action (SAS URI of the disk), DBforPostgreSQL flexibleServers/write and Sql servers/databases/write (restoring into the orchestrator subscription), Insights/DiagnosticSettings/write and Storage listkeys/action.

quotes: The orchestrator subscription requires the target role to scan the data stores. The role is assigned at the monitoring scope or target subscriptions level
| Microsoft.Compute/disks/beginGetAccess/action | Monitored Subscriptions | Actions | To get the SAS URI of the disk |
| Microsoft.DBforPostgreSQL/flexibleServers/write | Monitored Subscriptions | Actions | To restore the PostgreSQL Flexible Server into the Orchestrator subscription |
| Microsoft.Sql/servers/databases/write | Monitored Subscriptions | Actions | To restore the SQL server into the Orchestrator subscription |
| Microsoft.Insights/DiagnosticSettings/write | Monitored Subscriptions | Actions | To create a diagnostic setting for Azure storage accounts |
| Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/listkeys/action | Monitored Subscriptions | Actions | To read Azure storage account keys |

target-role-dataactions.statement: The Target Role DataActions include Key Vault keys/read, keys/unwrap/action and keys/wrap/action, Storage blobServices/*/read, and Key Vault secrets/getSecret/action, which is conditional and required only if Custom Network is used with Unmanaged DB Scanning.

quotes: | Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/keys/read | Monitored Subscriptions | DataActions | To list the keys in a specified vault |
| Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/keys/unwrap/action | Monitored Subscriptions | DataActions | To unwrap a symmetric key with a Key Vault key |
| Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/keys/wrap/action | Monitored Subscriptions | DataActions | To wrap a symmetric key with a Key Vault key |
| Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/blobServices/*/read | Monitored Subscriptions | DataActions | To read blobs from containers |

| Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/secrets/getSecret/action | Monitored Subscriptions | DataActions | To get the value of a secret This permission is conditional and only required if Custom Network is used with Unmanaged DB Scanning. |

orchestrator-role-scope.statement: The Orchestrator Role is used by the orchestrator instance to scan data and is assigned at the DSPM resource group level; among its permissions it creates snapshots and virtual machines for scanning, the PostgreSQL flexible server and SQL server for scanning, and the private endpoint for scanning.

quotes: The orchestrator instance requires this role to scan the data. The role is assigned at the DSPM resource group level
| Microsoft.Compute/snapshots/write | DSPM resource group | Actions | To create a snapshot |
| Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/write | DSPM resource group | Actions | To create a virtual machine for scanning |

orchestrator-role-conditional-mip.statement: In the Orchestrator Role, Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/extensions/write is conditional and required only if Custom Network is selected; the Storage DataActions that write MIP labeled files and the file backup semantics privilege are scoped to Monitored Subscriptions.

quotes: | Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/extensions/write | DSPM resource group | Actions | To create virtual machine extension This permission is conditional and only required if Custom Network is selected. |
| Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/fileServices/fileshares/files/write | Monitored Subscriptions | DataActions | To write MIP labeled files |
| Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/fileServices/writeFileBackupSemantics/action | Monitored Subscriptions | DataActions | To write file backup semantics privilege |

mip-api-permissions.statement: MIP labeling needs these application permissions on the Orchestrator Managed Identity: Azure Rights Management Services Content.Writer, Microsoft Information Protection Sync Service UnifiedPolicy.Tenant.Read, and Microsoft Graph InformationProtectionPolicy.Read.All.

quotes: The following API permissions are required for MIP labeling:
| Azure Rights Management Services | Content.Writer | Orchestrator Managed Identity | Application | To create protected content |
| Microsoft Information Protection Sync Service | UnifiedPolicy.Tenant.Read | Orchestrator Managed Identity | Application | To read all unified policies of the tenant |
| Microsoft Graph | InformationProtectionPolicy.Read.All | Orchestrator Managed Identity | Application | To read all published labels and label policies for an organization |

scanner-role.statement: The Scanner Role is used by scanner instances launched in the orchestrator subscription, assigned at the DSPM resource group level, with Key Vault secrets/getSecret/action and Storage blobServices/*/read DataActions.

quotes: The scanner role is used by the scanner instances that are launched in the orchestrator subscription to perform data scanning. The role is assigned at the DSPM resource group level
| Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/secrets/getSecret/action | DSPM resource group | DataActions | To get the value of a secret |
| Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/blobServices/*/read | DSPM resource group | DataActions | To read blobs from containers |

custom-network-role.statement: The Custom Network Configuration Role lists, at the subscription level for the orchestrator, networkSecurityGroups/join/action, virtualNetworks/subnets/join/action and subnets/joinViaServiceEndpoint/action on the orchestrator subscription; these permissions are conditional and required only if Custom Network is selected.

quotes: To configure a custom network in your organization, the orchestrator requires the following roles and permissions at the subscription level
These permissions are conditional and only required if Custom Network is selected.
| Microsoft.Network/networkSecurityGroups/join/action | Orchestrator Subscription | Actions | To join the Network Security Group of the Custom Network mode |
| Microsoft.Network/virtualNetworks/subnets/join/action | Orchestrator Subscription | Actions | To join the subnet of the Custom Network |
| Microsoft.Network/virtualNetworks/subnets/joinViaServiceEndpoint/action | Orchestrator Subscription | Actions | To join the SQL database to a subnet of the Custom Network |

encryption-role.statement: The Encryption Role is used by the Local Scanner Platform for CMK encryption tasks on instances, at the DSPM resource group scope, and includes Key Vault keys/decrypt/action and keys/encrypt/action.

quotes: This role is used by the Local Scanner Platform to perform the CMK encryption related tasks on instances.
| Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/keys/decrypt/action | DSPM resource group | DataActions | To decrypt ciphertext with a key |
| Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/keys/encrypt/action | DSPM resource group | DataActions | To encrypt plaintext with a key |

ai-agent-role.statement: The Custom Role (AI Agent) collects data from AI services and is assigned to the Tree Discovery service principal for each subscription; it is required only when AI service data collection is enabled and is assigned at the subscription level, not the root management group.

quotes: The custom role is required to collect data from AI services. Assign this role to the Tree Discovery service principal, created by the Tree Discovery template, for each subscription.
This role is required only when AI service data collection is enabled.
Assign the role at the subscription level, not the root management group.

ai-agent-permissions.statement: Among the permissions the AI Agent role lists are Microsoft.MachineLearningServices/workspaces/*/read (with Type notActions) and DataActions to read OpenAI assistants, thread runs and vector stores and Microsoft.CognitiveServices/accounts/AIServices/agents/read.

sp-api-permissions.statement: The IAM roles and permissions page lists as required for the DSPM service principal in Microsoft Entra ID, without naming an onboarding type, the Application permissions Application.Read.All, AuditLog.Read.All, Directory.Read.All, InformationProtectionPolicy.Read.All, Organization.Read.All, Reports.Read.All, RoleManagement.Read.Directory, RoleManagementPolicy.Read.Directory and UserAuthenticationMethod.Read.All, plus the Delegate permission User.Read.

quotes: The following API permissions are required for the DSPM service principal registered in Microsoft Entra ID:
| Application.Read.All | Application | To read all applications |
| AuditLog.Read.All | Application | To read all audit log data |
| Directory.Read.All | Application | To read directory data |
| InformationProtectionPolicy.Read.All | Application | To read all published labels and label policies for an organization |
| Organization.Read.All | Application | To read organization information |
| Reports.Read.All | Application | To read all usage reports |
| RoleManagement.Read.Directory | Application | To read all directory RBAC settings |
| RoleManagementPolicy.Read.Directory | Application | To read all policies for privileged role assignments of your company's directory |
| UserAuthenticationMethod.Read.All | Application | To read all users' authentication methods |
| User.Read | Delegate | To sign in and read user profile |

sp-graph-permissions-required.summary: The IAM roles page lists ten Microsoft Graph permissions as required for the DSPM service principal and names no onboarding type; the subscription onboarding page marks eight of them Optional.

positions.says: The API permissions listed, including AuditLog.Read.All, are required for the DSPM service principal.

quotes: The following API permissions are required for the DSPM service principal registered in Microsoft Entra ID:
| AuditLog.Read.All | Application | To read all audit log data |

positions.says: In subscription onboarding AuditLog.Read.All is Optional.

quotes: | AuditLog.Read.All | Optional | Application | Read all audit log data |
Entitlements are affected if the optional API permissions are not configured.

sp-graph-permissions-required.impact: Whether all ten Graph permissions are needed depends on the page read; the IAM page does not say it is scoped to tenant or management group onboarding.

tenant-roles-table-garbled.title: Which scope each tenant prerequisite role carries
tenant-roles-table-garbled.detail: The tenant prerequisites table is garbled in the capture: the Key Vault Administrator text sits inside one cell and the Orchestrator subscription cell follows it, so which scope each role carries is not reliably stated. The claim tenant-azure-roles reads the rows as they appear, including the shifted row '| User Access Administrator | Management group |  |', and does not state the Key Vault Administrator scope.

cleanup-trigger.title: When the tenant cleanup procedure applies
cleanup-trigger.detail: The cleanup procedure in the tenant prerequisites (delete resource groups, purge key vaults, delete roles and the service principal, rerun the Tree Discovery and Azure Onboarding templates) has no heading in the capture, so its trigger is unstated; only the resource names are claimed (tenant-cleanup-resources).

name-and-tag-rules.title: Storage account name characters
name-and-tag-rules.detail: The storage account name limit is 16 characters with no stated allowed characters or minimum. The Azure custom tag key and value rules are in [[dspm.cloud-accounts:tags-azure]]; only the Private DNS zone limit of 15 is captured besides the name limit.

terraform-templates-not-vendored.title: Contents of the downloaded Terraform templates
terraform-templates-not-vendored.detail: The downloaded Terraform templates (backend.tf, azure_tf_basic.tf, terraform.tfvars with random_seed and primary_region) are not vendored, so their contents are unchecked. No API, SDK or Terraform-provider surface for DSPM was checked here.
